sanskrit: upaviṣṭās tu te sarve yasmin prāyaṃ giristhale harayo gṛdhrarājaś ca taṃ deśam upacakrame
english: While all those monkeys sat fasting at the mountain place prepared for death, the king of vultures approached that very spot.

sanskrit: sāmpātir nāma nāmnā tu cirajīvī vihaṃgamaḥ bhrātā jaṭāyuṣaḥ śrīmān prakhyātabalapauruṣaḥ
english: That long-lived bird was named Sampāti, splendid and renowned for his strength and valor — the elder brother of Jaṭāyu.

sanskrit: kandarād abhiniṣkramya sa vindhyasya mahāgireḥ upaviṣṭān harīn dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭātmā giram abravīt
english: Emerging from a cave of the great Vindhya mountain and seeing the monkeys seated there, he spoke with a delighted heart.

sanskrit: vidhiḥ kila naraṃ loke vidhānenānuvartate yathāyaṃ vihito bhakṣyaś cirān mahyam upāgataḥ
english: "Fate in this world surely follows its own ordinance — how fitting that this destined prey has come to me at last after so long."

sanskrit: paramparāṇāṃ bhakṣiṣye vānarāṇāṃ mṛtaṃ mṛtam uvācaivaṃ vacaḥ pakṣī tān nirīkṣya plavaṃgamān
english: "I shall devour these monkeys one by one as they die, each in turn" — so the bird spoke, gazing upon those leaping creatures.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bhakṣalubdhasya pakṣiṇaḥ aṅgadaḥ param āyasto hanūmantam athābravīt
english: Hearing the words of that bird hungry for prey, Aṅgada, greatly distressed, then spoke to Hanūmān.

sanskrit: paśya sītāpadeśena sākṣād vaivasvato yamaḥ imaṃ deśam anuprāpto vānarāṇāṃ vipattaye
english: "Look — under the pretext of Sītā, Yama, the son of Vivasvān himself, has come to this place for the destruction of us monkeys."

sanskrit: rāmasya na kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ rājño na ca vacaḥ kṛtam harīṇām iyam ajñātā vipattiḥ sahasāgatā
english: "Rāma's task has not been accomplished, the king's command has not been fulfilled — this unforeseen calamity has suddenly come upon the monkeys."

sanskrit: vaidehyāḥ priyakāmena kṛtaṃ karma jaṭāyuṣā gṛdhrarājena yat tatra śrutaṃ vas tad aśeṣataḥ
english: "The deed done by Jaṭāyu, the king of vultures, out of love for Vaidehī — all of that you have already heard in full."

sanskrit: tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni tiryagyonigatāny api priyaṃ kurvanti rāmasya tyaktvā prāṇān yathā vayam
english: "Even so, all beings — even those born into animal wombs — do Rāma's bidding, abandoning their lives just as we ourselves do."

sanskrit: rāghavārthe pariśrāntā vayaṃ saṃtyaktajīvitāḥ kāntārāṇi prapannāḥ sma na ca paśyāma maithilīm
english: "Exhausted in the service of Rāghava, we have given up our lives; we entered the wilderness — yet we have not found the princess of Mithilā."

sanskrit: sa sukhī gṛdhrarājas tu rāvaṇena hato raṇe muktaś ca sugrīvabhayād gataś ca paramāṃ gatim
english: "That king of vultures is fortunate — slain in battle by Rāvaṇa, he was freed from all fear of Sugrīva and has attained the highest state."

sanskrit: jaṭāyuṣo vināśena rājño daśarathasya ca haraṇena ca vaidehyāḥ saṃśayaṃ harayo gatāḥ
english: "By the destruction of Jaṭāyu, by the death of King Daśaratha, and by the abduction of Vaidehī, the monkeys have fallen into peril."

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇayor vāsām araṇye saha sītayā rāghavasya ca bāṇena vālinaś ca tathā vadhaḥ
english: "The forest-dwelling of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together with Sītā, and likewise the slaying of Vālin by Rāghava's arrow —"

sanskrit: rāmakopād aśeṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ tathā vadhaḥ kaikeyyā varadānena idaṃ hi vikṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: "And the total destruction of the rākṣasas through Rāma's wrath — all this calamity has been wrought by the boon granted to Kaikeyī."

sanskrit: tat tu śrutvā tadā vākyam aṅgadasya mukhodgatam abravīd vacanaṃ gṛdhras tīkṣṇatuṇḍo mahāsvanaḥ
english: Upon hearing those words uttered from Aṅgada's mouth, the vulture with his sharp beak spoke in a loud voice.

sanskrit: ko 'yaṃ girā ghoṣayati prāṇaiḥ priyatarasya me jaṭāyuṣo vadhaṃ bhrātuḥ kampayann iva me manaḥ
english: "Who is this who proclaims with his voice the slaying of my brother Jaṭāyu, dearer to me than life itself, making my heart tremble?"

sanskrit: katham āsīj janasthāne yuddhaṃ rākṣasagṛdhrayoḥ nāmadheyam idaṃ bhrātuś cirasyādya mayā śrutam
english: "How did the battle between the rākṣasa and the vulture take place at Janasthāna? After so long, I hear today this name of my brother."

sanskrit: yavīyaso guṇajñasya ślāghanīyasya vikramaiḥ tad iccheyam ahaṃ śrotuṃ vināśaṃ vānararṣabhāḥ
english: "I wish to hear the end of my younger brother — he who knew virtue and was praiseworthy for his valor. Tell me, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: bhrātur jaṭāyuṣas tasya janasthānanivāsinaḥ tasyaiva ca mama bhrātuḥ sakhā daśarathaḥ katham yasya rāmaḥ priyaḥ putro jyeṣṭho gurujanapriyaḥ
english: "My brother Jaṭāyu dwelt at Janasthāna, and Daśaratha was that very brother's dear friend — he whose beloved eldest son Rāma is devoted to his elders. How did this come to pass?"

sanskrit: sūryāṃśudagdhapakṣatvān na śaknomi visarpitum iccheyaṃ parvatād asmād avatartum ariṃdamāḥ
english: "Since my wings were burned by the rays of the sun, I cannot spread them; I wish to descend from this mountain, O destroyers of enemies."

sanskrit: śokād bhraṣṭasvaram api śrutvā te hariyūthapāḥ śraddadhur naiva tad vākyaṃ karmaṇā tasya śaṅkitāḥ
english: Though the leaders of the monkey troops heard those words — his voice broken by grief — they did not trust them at all, suspicious of his intentions.

sanskrit: te prāyam upaviṣṭās tu dṛṣṭvā gṛdhraṃ plavaṃgamāḥ cakrur buddhiṃ tadā raudrāṃ sarvān no bhakṣayiṣyati
english: Those monkeys, seated in their fast unto death, saw the vulture and formed this terrible thought: "He will devour all of us."

sanskrit: sarvathā prāyam āsīnān yadi no bhakṣayiṣyati kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṣipraṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ
english: "If he eats us while we sit here fasting in any case, we shall have achieved our purpose — swiftly obtaining release from this place."

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ tataś cakruḥ sarve te vānararṣabhāḥ avatārya gireḥ śṛṅgād gṛdhram āhāṅgadas tadā
english: After all those foremost monkeys formed this resolve, Aṅgada then addressed the vulture who had descended from the mountain peak.

sanskrit: babhūvur kṣarajo nāma vānarendraḥ pratāpavān mamāryaḥ pārthivaḥ pakṣin dhārmikau tasya cātmajau
english: "There was a powerful lord of monkeys named Kṣaraja — he was my noble king, O bird, and righteous were both of his sons."

sanskrit: sugrīvaś caiva valī ca putrāv oghabalāv ubhau loke viśrutakarmābhūd rājā vālī pitā mama
english: "Sugrīva and Vālin — both sons endowed with torrential strength. King Vālin, renowned throughout the world for his deeds, was my father."

sanskrit: rājā kṛtsnasya jagata ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahārathaḥ rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmān praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam
english: "Rāma the son of Daśaratha, the great warrior and splendid king of the entire world among the Ikṣvākus, entered the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā pitur nideśanirato dharmyaṃ panthānam āśritaḥ tasya bhāryā janasthānād rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt
english: "Together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife Vaidehī, devoted to his father's command and treading the righteous path — his wife was forcibly abducted from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: rāmasya ca pitur mitraṃ jaṭāyur nāma gṛdhrarāṭ dadarśa sītāṃ vaidehīṃ hriyamāṇāṃ vihāyasā
english: "Jaṭāyu the vulture-lord, a friend of Rāma's father, saw Sītā Vaidehī being carried away through the sky."

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ virathaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayitvā ca maithilīm pariśrāntaś ca vṛddhaś ca rāvaṇena hato raṇe
english: "He made Rāvaṇa chariotless and caused Maithilī to be set down — but exhausted and old, he was slain in battle by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: evaṃ gṛdhro hatas tena rāvaṇena bahīyasā saṃskṛtaś cāpi rāmeṇa gataś ca gatim uttamām
english: "Thus that vulture, slain by the mighty Rāvaṇa, was duly cremated by Rāma and attained the highest destination."

sanskrit: tato mama pitṛvyeṇa sugrīveṇa mahātmanā cakāra rāghavaḥ sakhyaṃ so 'vadhīt pitaraṃ mama
english: "Then Rāghava formed a friendship with Sugrīva, my great-souled paternal uncle — and he slew my father Vālin."

sanskrit: māma pitrā viruddho hi sugrīvaḥ sacivaiḥ saha nihatya vālinaṃ rāmas tatas tam abhiṣecayat
english: "For Sugrīva, estranged from my father, together with his ministers — after slaying Vālin, Rāma then consecrated Sugrīva as king."

sanskrit: sa rājye sthāpitas tena sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ rājā vānaramukhyānāṃ yena prasthāpitā vayam
english: "That Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, was installed in the kingdom by Rāma as king of the foremost monkeys — and it is he who dispatched us."

sanskrit: evaṃ rāmaprayuktās tu mārgamāṇās tatas tataḥ vaidehīṃ nādhigacchāmo rātrau sūryaprabhām iva
english: "Thus sent forth by Rāma, searching here and there, we have not found Vaidehī — like seeking the sun's radiance in the night."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ daṇdakāraṇyaṃ vicitya susamāhitāḥ ajñānāt tu praviṣṭāḥ sma dharaṇyā vivṛtaṃ bilam
english: "We searched the Daṇḍaka forest carefully — and then, unknowingly, we entered a cave that had opened in the earth."

sanskrit: mayasya māyā vihitaṃ tad bilaṃ ca vicinvatām vyatītas tatra no māso yo rājñā sāmayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "That cave was fashioned by Maya's magic, and while we searched within it, the month that the king had fixed as our deadline passed."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ kapirājasya sarve vacanakāriṇaḥ kṛtāṃ saṃsthām atikrāntā bhayāt prāyam upāsmahe
english: "We, who are all subject to the monkey-king's command, have exceeded the appointed time — and so out of fear we undertake this fast unto death."

sanskrit: kruddhe tasmiṃs tu kākutsthe sugrīve ca salakṣmaṇe gatānām api sarveṣāṃ tatra no nāsti jīvitam
english: "With Kākutstha Rāma angry, and Sugrīva together with Lakṣmaṇa wrathful, there is no life for us even if we were to return — so we have resolved to die here."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ vānarais tyaktajīvitaiḥ sabāṣpo vānarān gṛdhraḥ pratyuvāca mahāsvanaḥ
english: Thus addressed with piteous words by the monkeys who had abandoned hope of life, the vulture, with tears in his eyes, replied to the monkeys in a great voice.

sanskrit: yavīyān mama sa bhrātā jaṭāyur nāma vānarāḥ yamākhyāta hataṃ yuddhe rāvaṇena balīyasā
english: "That younger brother of mine named Jaṭāyu, whom you have told me was slain in battle by the powerful Rāvaṇa —"

sanskrit: vṛddhabhāvād apakṣatvāc chṛṇvaṃs tad api marṣaye na hi me śaktir adyāsti bhrātur vairavimokṣaṇe
english: "On account of old age and my winglessness, even hearing this I must endure it — for I have no strength today to avenge my brother's enemy."

sanskrit: purā vṛtravadhe vṛtte sa cāhaṃ ca jayaiṣiṇau ādityam upayātau svo jvalantaṃ raśmimālinam
english: "Long ago, when the slaying of Vṛtra had occurred, both he and I, eager for victory, flew up toward the blazing sun wreathed in rays."

sanskrit: āvṛtyākāśamārgeṇa javena sma gatau bhṛśam madhyaṃ prāpte ca sūrye ca jaṭāyur avasīdati
english: "Covering the path through the sky with great speed we flew — but when the sun reached its zenith, Jaṭāyu began to sink."

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryaraśmibhir arditam pakṣābhyaṃ chādayām āsa snehāt paramavihvalam
english: "Seeing that brother of mine tormented by the sun's rays and utterly overwhelmed, out of affection I shielded him with my wings."

sanskrit: nirdagdhapakṣaḥ patito vindhye 'haṃ vānarottamāḥ aham asmin vasan bhrātuḥ pravṛttiṃ nopalakṣaye
english: "My wings scorched and burned, I fell upon the Vindhya, O best of monkeys — and dwelling here, I have had no news of my brother."

sanskrit: jaṭāyuṣas tv evam ukto bhrātrā saṃpātinā tadā yuvarājo mahāprājñaḥ pratyuvācāṅgadas tadā
english: When Sampāti had spoken thus of Jaṭāyu, the crown prince Aṅgada of great wisdom then replied.

sanskrit: jaṭāyuṣo yadi bhrātā śrutaṃ te gaditaṃ mayā ākhyāhi yadi jānāsi nilayaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: "If you are truly the brother of Jaṭāyu, you have heard what I have told you — now tell us, if you know, the abode of that rākṣasa."

sanskrit: adīrghadarśinaṃ taṃ vā rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam antike yadi vā dūre yadi jānāsi śaṃsa naḥ
english: "That Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, who is lacking in foresight — whether nearby or far, if you know, inform us."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejā jyeṣṭho bhrātā jaṭāyuṣaḥ ātmānurūpaṃ vacanaṃ vānarān saṃpraharṣayan
english: Then the elder brother of Jaṭāyu, blazing with great energy, spoke words befitting his own nature, filling the monkeys with joy.

sanskrit: nirdagdhapakṣo gṛdhro 'haṃ gatavīryaḥ plavaṃgamāḥ vāṅmātreṇa tu rāmasya kariṣye sāhyam uttamam
english: "Though I am a vulture with scorched wings and diminished strength, O leaping ones, I will render supreme aid to Rāma — at least by means of speech."

sanskrit: jānāmi vāruṇāl lokān viṣṇos traivikramān api devāsuravimardāṃś ca amṛtasya ca manthanam
english: "I know the worlds of Varuṇa and the three strides of Viṣṇu as well; I know the battles of gods and asuras, and the churning of the nectar."

sanskrit: rāmasya yad idaṃ kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ prathamaṃ mayā jarayā ca hṛtaṃ tejaḥ prāṇāś ca śithilā mama
english: "As for this task of Rāma's, it should have been done first by me — but old age has stolen my vigor and my life-breath is weakened."

sanskrit: taruṇī rūpasaṃpannā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā hriyamāṇā mayā dṛṣṭā rāvaṇena durātmanā
english: "I saw a young woman of perfect beauty, adorned with all ornaments, being carried off by Rāvaṇa, that wicked-souled one."

sanskrit: krośantī rāma rāmeti lakṣmaṇeti ca bhāminī bhūṣaṇāny apavidhyantī gātrāṇi ca vidhunvatī
english: "She was crying out 'Rāma! Rāma!' and 'Lakṣmaṇa!' — that radiant woman, flinging off her ornaments and writhing her limbs."

sanskrit: sūryaprabheva śailāgre tasyāḥ kauśeyam uttamam asite rākṣase bhāti yathā vā taḍidambude
english: "Her finest silk garment, like the sun's glow atop a mountain, shone against that dark rākṣasa as lightning blazes against a rain cloud."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu sītām ahaṃ manye rāmasya parikīrtanāt śrūyatāṃ me kathayato nilayaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: "By the mention of Rāma's name, I believe that woman is Sītā. Now hear from me as I describe the dwelling of that rākṣasa."

sanskrit: putro viśravasaḥ sākṣād bhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca adhyāste nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇo nāma rākasaḥ
english: "The rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa — the own son of Viśravas and brother of Vaiśravaṇa — dwells in the city of Laṅkā."

sanskrit: ito dvīpe samudrasya saṃpūrṇe śatayojane tasmiṃl laṅkā purī ramyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā
english: "From here, a full hundred yojanas across the ocean on an island, the lovely city of Laṅkā was built by Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vasati vaidehī dīnā kauśeyavāsinī rāvaṇāntaḥpure ruddhā rākṣasībhiḥ surakṣitā
english: "In that city dwells Vaidehī, wretched, wearing silk, confined in Rāvaṇa's inner quarters and closely guarded by rākṣasī women."

sanskrit: janakasyātmajāṃ rājñas tasyāṃ drakṣyatha maithilīm laṅkāyām atha guptāyāṃ sāgareṇa samantataḥ
english: "You will behold that Maithilī, the daughter of King Janaka, there in Laṅkā — protected on all sides by the ocean."

sanskrit: saṃprāpya sāgarasyāntaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ śatayojanam āsādya dakṣiṇaṃ kūlaṃ tato drakṣyatha rāvaṇam
english: "Reaching the ocean's far shore, a full hundred yojanas away, and arriving at the southern bank, you will there behold Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: tatraiva tvaritāḥ kṣipraṃ vikramadhvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ jñānena khalu paśyāmi dṛṣṭvā pratyāgamiṣyatha
english: "Make haste there at once and strive with valor, O leaping ones! I truly see this with my inner sight — having found her, you will return."

sanskrit: ādyaḥ panthāḥ kuliṅgānāṃ ye cānye dhānyajīvinaḥ dvitīyo balibhojānāṃ ye ca vṛkṣaphalāśinaḥ
english: "The first path belongs to the sparrows and those other birds that live on grain; the second to the crows and those that eat tree-fruits."

sanskrit: bhāsās tṛtīyaṃ gacchanti krauñcāś ca kuraraiḥ saha śyenāś caturthaṃ gacchanti gṛdhrā gacchanti pañcamam
english: "The bhāsa birds travel the third path, and the krauñcas together with the kurara birds; hawks travel the fourth, and vultures travel the fifth."

sanskrit: balavīryopapannānāṃ rūpayauvanaśālinām ṣaṣṭhas tu panthā haṃsānāṃ vainateyagatiḥ parā vainateyāc ca no janma sarveṣāṃ vānararṣabhāḥ
english: "The sixth path belongs to the swans endowed with strength, valor, beauty, and youth — and beyond that is the way of Vainateya Garuḍa. From Vainateya descends the lineage of all of us, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: garhitaṃ tu kṛtaṃ karma yena sma piśitāśanāḥ ihastho 'haṃ prapaśyāmi rāvaṇaṃ jānakīṃ tathā
english: "A reprehensible deed was done by which we became flesh-eaters — yet even standing here, I behold Rāvaṇa and Jānakī with my sight."

sanskrit: asmākam api sauvarṇaṃ divyaṃ cakṣurbalaṃ tathā tasmād āhāravīryeṇa nisargeṇa ca vānarāḥ āyojanaśatāt sāgrād vayaṃ paśyāma nityaśaḥ
english: "We too possess a divine golden power of vision — and so by the power of our sustenance and by our very nature, O monkeys, we always see as far as a full hundred yojanas and more."

sanskrit: asmākaṃ vihitā vṛttir nisārgeṇa ca dūrataḥ vihitā pādamūle tu vṛttiś caraṇayodhinām
english: "Our livelihood is ordained by nature to be found at a distance; the livelihood of those who fight on foot is ordained to be found at their very feet."

sanskrit: upāyo dṛśyatāṃ kaś cil laṅghane lavaṇāmbhasaḥ abhigamya tu vaidehīṃ samṛddhārthā gamiṣyatha
english: "Let some means be found for crossing the salt ocean — having reached Vaidehī, you will return with your purpose fulfilled."

sanskrit: samudraṃ netum icchāmi bhavadbhir varuṇālayam pradāsyāmy udakaṃ bhrātuḥ svargatasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "I wish to go with you to the ocean, abode of Varuṇa — I will offer water for my great-souled brother who has gone to heaven."

sanskrit: tato nītvā tu taṃ deśaṃ tīre nadanadīpateḥ nirdagdhapakṣaṃ saṃpātiṃ vānarāḥ sumahaujasaḥ
english: Then those mighty monkeys of great valor, having carried Sampāti — his wings burned away — to the shore of the lord of rivers and streams,

sanskrit: punaḥ pratyānayitvā vai taṃ deśaṃ patageśvaram babhūvur vānarā hṛṣṭāḥ pravṛttim upalabhya te
english: brought back that lord of birds to that very place; and the monkeys became filled with joy, having obtained this news to act upon.
